To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Facebook is a better social media tool for knowledge management than blogs.
Facebook and blogs can be used as tools for knowledge management, with Facebook being more suitable for knowledge sharing and knowledge creation.
Facebook is more effective in knowledge sharing, knowledge application and social support than blogs, and blogs are more effective in capturing new knowledge than Facebook.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of blogs and Facebook as knowledge management tools and their potential to enhance the learning experience in internship.
the potential and challenges of social media as tools to support knowledge sharing and management.
the potential of social media in supporting knowledge management and its implications on users' practices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both Facebook and blogs are effective in facilitating users' online knowledge management.
blogs and Facebook are complementary in their support of knowledge management processes.
Facebook is more conducive to the knowledge capture, sharing, and application of users.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Facebook has a greater potential in knowledge management than blogs, and it would be a good practice for knowledge management to use Facebook as the platform.
blogs and Facebook are two distinct social media platforms, which support users in different ways.
blogs and Facebook are useful tools to support knowledge management processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Facebook can serve as a more suitable social platform to support knowledge management in online environments.
the use of social media platforms such as blogs and Facebook can be used to support knowledge sharing and management among users in a collaborative work environment.
